kings1.7.p1.b1.text: Solomon, however, took thirteen years to complete the construction of his entire palace.

kings1.7.p1.b2.text: He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high …

kings1.7.p1.b3.text: In addition, he built a hall for the throne, the Hall of Justice, where he was to judge. It was paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling.

kings1.7.p1.b4.text: … He also made a palace like this hall for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom he had married.

kings1.7.p2.b1.text: All these buildings were constructed with costly stones, cut to size and trimmed with saws inside and out …

kings1.7.p2.b2.text: Now King Solomon sent to bring Huram from Tyre.

kings1.7.p2.b3.text: He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a craftsman in bronze. Huram had great skill, understanding, and knowledge for every kind of bronze work. …

kings1.7.p2.b4.text: … So he came to King Solomon and carried out all his work.

kings1.7.p3.b1.text: He cast two pillars of bronze, each eighteen cubits high and twelve cubits in circumference.

kings1.7.p3.b2.text: Likewise, he made the pillars with two rows of pomegranates around each grating to cover each capital atop the pillars.

kings1.7.p3.b3.text: Thus he set up the pillars at the portico of the temple. The pillar to the south he named Jachin, and the pillar to the north he named Boaz.

kings1.7.p4.b1.text: He also made the Sea of cast metal. It was circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim, five cubits in height, and thirty cubits in circumference.

kings1.7.p4.b2.text: It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was fashioned like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. …

kings1.7.p4.b3.text: The Sea stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. …

kings1.7.p4.b4.text: … It could hold two thousand baths.

kings1.7.p5.b1.text: In addition, he made ten movable stands of bronze, each four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.

kings1.7.p5.b2.text: … on the panels between the uprights were lions, oxen, and cherubim. …

kings1.7.p5.b3.text: The wheels were made like chariot wheels; …

kings1.7.p5.b4.text: He set five stands on the south side of the temple and five on the north, …

kings1.7.p6.b1.text: The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan between Succoth and Zarethan.

kings1.7.p6.b2.text: Additionally, Huram made the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls. So Huram finished all the work that he had undertaken for King Solomon in the house of the LORD:

kings1.7.p6.b3.text: Solomon left all these articles unweighed, because there were so many. The weight of the bronze could not be determined.

kings1.7.p7.b1.text: Solomon also made all the furnishings for the house of the LORD: the golden altar; the golden table on which was placed the Bread of the Presence;

kings1.7.p7.b2.text: the lampstands of pure gold in front of the inner sanctuary, five on the right side and five on the left; the gold flowers, lamps, and tongs;

kings1.7.p7.b3.text: the pure gold basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, ladles, and censers; and the gold hinges for the doors of the inner temple (that is, the Most Holy Place ) as well as for the doors of the main hall of the temple.

kings1.7.p8.b1.text: So all the work that King Solomon had performed for the house of the LORD was completed. Then Solomon brought in the items his father David had dedicated—the silver, the gold, and the furnishings—and he placed them in the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
